name: obol_flag_hunt_2026_09
description: Thorough post-foothold flag capture, split the way the exam scores it: the LOCAL/user flag from any shell, and the ROOT/proof flag once you have administrative access. Each flag is captured next to a host-identity command (for the screenshot) and recorded as its own objective, so grabbing the user flag never hides the still-open root flag.

source.name: O.B.O.L flag capture methodology
source.notes: A captured flag is proof, not a checkbox. Local and root are separate objectives (objective.local_flag / objective.root_flag) so the coach keeps prompting for the one you have not captured yet.

actions.title: Capture the User Flag (Linux)
actions.hypothesis: ANY Linux shell can read the user flag - a reverse shell or webshell reads user.txt/local.txt as readily as an SSH login, no credential required. Grab it first and mark the local objective done; the root flag is its own step once you escalate.

report.finding: Captured the local/user flag from the Linux foothold.

commands.note: IN YOUR SHELL (no credential needed): find every flag file and print the user flag with your identity for the screenshot. The common case — you do not need SSH creds to read a flag you can already reach.
commands.run: id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; find / -xdev -type f -size -4k \( {{flag_inames_linux}} \) 2>/dev/null -exec echo '--- {} ---' \; -exec cat {} \;

commands.note: LOCATE OVER SSH (only if you hold SSH creds and have no shell yet). A one-liner from Kali, so it only LOCATES; OffSec scores a flag read this way ZERO. Paste the output back and obol records the path; capture it on the host next.

ON THE HOST, capture the LOCAL/user flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE your shell and screenshot the whole frame: id + ip addr (the target IP) + the flag, together. obol records this as the captured local flag.
commands.run: id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_local}}

actions.title: Capture the Root Flag (Linux)
actions.hypothesis: You have root - capture the proof flag before anything else so you can mark the box's final objective done. It lives in /root, which only root can read; grab it with your identity for the screenshot, then move on (persistence, pivot, loot) knowing the box is owned.

report.finding: Captured the root/proof flag from the Linux host.

commands.note: ON THE HOST as root, capture the ROOT flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE your root shell and screenshot the whole frame together (id must show uid=0). obol records this as the captured root flag — the box's final objective.
commands.run: id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_root}}

commands.note: If the exact path was not located yet, sweep for it as root (now that /root is readable).

actions.title: Capture the User Flag (Windows)
actions.hypothesis: ANY Windows shell reads the user flag - a webshell, a WinRM session, or a service-exploit shell all read the user's Desktop\local.txt, no credential required. Grab it first and mark the local objective done; the root/proof flag is its own step once you are SYSTEM/Administrator.

report.finding: Captured the local/user flag from the Windows foothold.

commands.note: WINRM INTERACTIVE SHELL (Recommended when port 5985 is open): Connect directly over WinRM with domain credentials. Once connected, locate and capture the user flag.
WINRM PASS-THE-HASH SHELL: Connect directly over WinRM with a captured NT hash.
IN-SESSION LOCATE FIRST: Inside your Evil-WinRM shell, recursively search user profiles to verify the exact path of user.txt. Paste the path it prints and obol fills the read below.
IN-SESSION PROOF READ: Display host identity, IP, and the flag in the same frame for the report screenshot. Ungates once the flag path is confirmed.
WINRM REMOTE LOCATE (When port 5985 is open): Search user profiles for the user flag remotely over WinRM in one command without opening an interactive shell.
commands.run: nxc winrm {{target}} -u '{{user}}' -p '{{password}}' -x 'Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Filter *user.txt -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName'

commands.note: WINRM REMOTE READ (When port 5985 is open): Read the confirmed user flag directly over WinRM in one shot from Kali.
WINRM REMOTE READ WITH NT HASH: Read the confirmed user flag over WinRM using pass-the-hash.

SMB DIRECT CAPTURE (low-privileged domain credential, no shell required): On domain networks with a readable Users share (e.g. Active), grab user.txt directly over SMB from the user's Desktop. Works even when WinRM is closed and without any code execution on the target. If tree connect fails (NT_STATUS_BAD_NETWORK_NAME), use evil-winrm.
LOCATE OVER SMB (from Kali): Spiders the Users share for flag files ending in .txt if the share exists.
REMOTE LOCATE OVER SMB: Searches every user profile Desktop over SMB. Note: Requires administrative execution rights on the target; if execution fails on non-admin accounts, use evil-winrm.

LAB QUICK GRAB (not OffSec-legal): with the dumped Administrator hash, search every user's Desktop and print the flag remotely in one shot, no shell. obol fills the hash from the NTDS dump, no credential swap, and the names from your profile.

actions.title: Capture the Root/Proof Flag (Windows)
actions.hypothesis: You are SYSTEM/Administrator - capture the proof flag (Administrator's Desktop\proof.txt / root.txt) before anything else so the box's final objective is done. Grab it with hostname + ipconfig for the screenshot, then move on to persistence/pivot knowing the box is owned.

report.finding: Captured the root/proof flag from the Windows host.

commands.note: PREFERRED REMOTE LOCATE (Instant Desktop Sweep with NT Hash over SMB): Scans every user profile Desktop for root/proof flags using the Administrator NT hash. Finishes in under 1 second. Paste output to ungate the flag read.

commands.run: nxc winrm {{target}} -u {{dauser}} -H {{dahash}} -x 'Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Filter *root*.txt -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName'
commands.note: WINRM REMOTE LOCATE WITH NT HASH (When port 5985 is open): Fast PowerShell sweep over WinRM with the Administrator hash to find root/proof flags.
WMI REMOTE LOCATE WITH NT HASH: Sweep user profiles for root/proof flags over WMI using the Administrator NT hash.

PREFERRED REMOTE LOCATE (Instant Desktop Sweep over WMI): Scans every user profile Desktop for root/proof flags without scanning deep subdirectories when administrative password is known. Finishes in under 1 second. Paste output to ungate the flag read.
REMOTE LOCATE (Instant Desktop Sweep over SMB): Searches every user profile Desktop over SMB without traversing junction points or deep directories when administrative password is known.
PREFERRED SMB HASH READ: With the Administrator NT hash dumped from NTDS, read the located root flag remotely over SMB.
WINRM REMOTE READ WITH NT HASH: Read the located root flag over WinRM using the Administrator NT hash.
PREFERRED WMI EXECUTION (When WinRM is closed): Read the located root flag directly over WMI (port 135) with administrative credentials.
Remote read over SMB with administrative password.
Fallback remote read with the DA hash via impacket wmiexec.
WINRM PASS-THE-HASH SHELL (Recommended when port 5985 is open): Connect directly over WinRM with the Administrator NT hash.
WINRM INTERACTIVE SHELL: Connect directly over WinRM with administrative credentials.
ON-HOST POWERSHELL LOCATE: If you have an interactive shell, search Desktops for root/proof flag files in under 1 second. Paste the path it prints to ungate the read command below.
ON THE HOST as SYSTEM/Administrator, capture the ROOT/proof flag with its identity in the same frame (whoami + hostname + ipconfig + the flag) for the report.

ON-HOST ADS LOCATE (Alternate Data Streams): Lists files and hidden alternate data streams on the Administrator Desktop. If flag files are hidden in streams (e.g. filename.txt:root.txt:$DATA), dir /r exposes them.

commands.run: Get-Item 'C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\*' -Stream * | Where-Object { $_.Stream -ne ':$DATA' } | Select-Object FileName, Stream, Length
commands.note: POWERSHELL ADS LOCATE: Enumerates NTFS alternate data streams across all files in the Administrator desktop, filtering out the default :$DATA stream.
POWERSHELL ADS READ: Reads the contents of a hidden alternate data stream flag (e.g. -Stream root.txt).
